subject: FintechCo - Logging & Sensitive Data Redaction (post-call recap)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Raj Singh <raj.singh@fintechco.com>, Elena Gomez <elena.gomez@fintechco.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: FintechCo — Post-demo recap: logging & redaction follow-ups

Hi Raj / Elena — great to meet today. Quick recap and next steps from our call: 

Summary:
- FintechCo requirement: strict PII handling, EU data residency for logs, 90-day retention target, and aggressive redaction of request/response logs (including headers / trace IDs).
- Redwood capabilities: configurable logging levels per-route, automatic PII redaction + custom regex rules, regionally-scoped log storage for EU deployments, and options to disable request/response logging entirely for sensitive routes.

Action items I mentioned on the call (next steps):
1) I'll share our SOC2 summary and a short design doc describing our logging & redaction pipeline (attached).
2) Please confirm the list of data elements you consider PII (examples: full account numbers, SSNs, customer email, raw payment tokens) and whether hashed/pseudonymized values would be acceptable for traceability.
3) We should scope a short technical demo showing how we configure redaction rules and test them against sample traces — propose week of Mar 8.
4) We'll propose contract language for retention and logging controls and loop in Rishi for legal/contract review.

Notes on technical constraints (high level):
- We scrub common sensitive headers by default (Authorization, Cookie).
- Trace IDs can be redacted or deterministically hashed on ingestion so they’re usable for debugging without exposing raw values.
- For Hosted accounts, request/response logs are stored in the customer region if EU residency is requested; Dedicated/Private deployments can enforce zero retention for raw request text.

Attached: redwood_soc2_summary.pdf; logging-redaction-design.docx

Would you confirm the examples of PII to redact and whether hashed IDs are OK?

Thanks — Marissa

From: Raj Singh <raj.singh@fintechco.com>

Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 09:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: FintechCo — Post-demo recap: logging & redaction follow-ups

Thanks Marissa — good overview. A few clarifications from our security & compliance team: 

1) PII scope: please treat the following as PII that must never appear in readable logs: full PAN/account numbers, national IDs (SSN/NI), full customer email addresses, payment tokens, and internal customer identifiers that map to live accounts. Partial tokens (last 4) are fine.
2) Retention: we need the ability to cap retention at 90 days for any logs that contain derived identifiers. For Hosted deployments, we require EU-only storage for logs and audit trails.
3) Trace IDs: we want traceability but cannot accept raw trace IDs that include internal customer IDs. Deterministic hashing is acceptable if you can show it’s HMAC-based with a customer-controlled key.
4) Headers: in addition to Authorization/Cookie, please ensure any X-* headers that may contain user-identifying values (e.g., X-User-ID, X-Session-ID) are scrubbed by default or configurable to be scrubbed.

Can you confirm: a) whether Redwood supports customer-controlled HSM/KMS for hashing keys; b) what the default retention for Hosted logs is; and c) whether you can generate an export of redaction rule test results for our audit?

If you can confirm these points I’ll book the demo.

—Raj
Raj Singh
Head of Security Engineering | FintechCo
raj.singh@fintechco.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Raj Singh <raj.singh@fintechco.com>, Elena Gomez <elena.gomez@fintechco.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 27 Feb 2026 11:47:00 -0800
Subject: Re: FintechCo — Post-demo recap: logging & redaction follow-ups

Hi Raj — appreciate the specifics, answers below and included a couple of notes on implementation. See attachments for SOC2 summary and the more detailed logging-redaction-design doc.

Answers:
- Customer-controlled keys: yes — for Dedicated and Private customers we support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) that can be used for deterministic hashing/HMAC; for Hosted we offer BYOK via supported cloud KMS providers (region-limited).
- Default retention (Hosted): default request/response logs are retained for 30 days; you can configure shorter retention windows down to zero for specific routes.
- Redaction/audit exports: we can run and export redaction test results (sample traces + pass/fail for each rule) for audits — we produce a signed CSV/JSON report and store it in your region.

Implementation notes (high level):
- Redaction pipeline: incoming requests pass through a PII-detection layer (ML + rule-based). If a rule matches, the raw span is replaced with the redacted variant before it lands in persistent logs. We support: regex rules, token-level classifiers (PII model), and custom field-mapping rules.
- Headers & trace IDs: headers are scrubbed via configurable header allowlists/deny-lists. Trace IDs can be HMAC-hashed on ingest; the HMAC key can be customer-managed so raw values are unrecoverable by Redwood.
- Sampling & retention: for high-volume routes we recommend sampling (e.g., 1%) for full payload capture and applying redaction rules for sampled items; non-sampled requests can still emit metadata (status, latency) without payload text.
- For Dedicated/Private: we support a zero-logging mode where no request/response payloads are persisted beyond ephemeral buffers used for immediate processing.

Attachments: redwood_soc2_summary.pdf (SOC2 & data residency notes), logging-redaction-design.docx (detailed flow and example regex rules).

Next steps I propose:
- Schedule a 45-min redaction configuration demo (Mar 8–12) showing the UI and running the redaction rules against sample traces.
- I’ll draft suggested contract language for the retention and key-management items and loop Rishi for review.

Rishi / Stephanie — can you review the attached logging-redaction-design.docx and suggest contract-friendly wording (retention cap, BYOK/HSM clause, zero-logging option) so I can send a redline back to Raj next week?

Thanks,
Marissa

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 28 Feb 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: Proposed wording for FintechCo redaction & retention clause (please review)

Rishi / Steph — attaching the design doc and a first-pass contract snippet below. Please add legal/ops notes and any impact on SLA or pricing if we include zero-logging or BYOK.

Proposed contract snippet (draft):
"Redwood agrees to store all request/response logs for FintechCo only within the EU region and to limit retention of any logs containing or derived from personally identifiable information (PII) to no more than ninety (90) days, unless otherwise agreed in writing. Customer may elect deterministic hashing of trace identifiers using a customer-managed key (BYOK) such that raw identifiers are not recoverable by Redwood. Customer may also request per-route zero-persistence (no request/response payloads persisted) for any route that processes sensitive PII; Redwood will provide a configuration guide and any reasonable documentation needed for audit."

Please be brief — I want to get this to Raj by Mon so we can keep momentum.

Marissa
